seo_description: Free, open-source clipboard history for macOS that promotes the text you reuse to a Frequent list. Everything stays on your Mac: no accounts, no network.
hero_sub: ReuseRankClips counts what you copy and promotes the text you reuse into a Frequent list above your history. Press ⌘⇧V, pick a clip, and it pastes into the app you were using.
features_sub: A menu bar clipboard that sorts itself, keeps your data local, and stays out of your way.

features.title: Automatic promotion
features.desc: Each distinct text is counted every time it is copied or pasted back. At your threshold (3 by default, 2 to 20) it moves into Frequent, where it never expires.

features.title: Frequent above Recent
features.desc: The popup shows Frequent clips first with a use-count badge, then Recent. Rename, pin, demote or delete any clip from a right-click menu.

features.title: Global hotkey and search
features.desc: Open the popup with ⌘⇧V, or set your own shortcut. Type to filter by text or label, use the arrow keys to move, Return to paste, Escape to close.

features.title: Privacy-minded capture
features.desc: Items flagged as concealed or transient by password managers are skipped, as are clips from apps on your ignore list and anything over 1 MB.

features.title: Control over history
features.desc: Keep 50 to 1000 recent items and expire them after 1 day, 1 week, 30 days, 90 days or never. Frequent and pinned items are never removed.

features.title: Local-only storage
features.desc: Clips are saved as a JSON file on your Mac. The app makes no network connections and needs no account.

permissions_step: To paste directly into the app you were using, grant Accessibility access in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility; without it, the app copies the clip and you paste it yourself.

faq.q: Is ReuseRankClips really free and open source?
faq.a: Yes. It is released under the MIT license, and the full source is on GitHub. There are no accounts, subscriptions or paid tiers; an optional Support button opens a Ko-fi page if you want to chip in.

Only Accessibility, and it is optional. macOS requires it for the app to send the Command-V keystroke that pastes into your previous app. If you decline, clips are still copied to the clipboard for you to paste manually. The app asks for no other permissions.

In a single JSON file at ~/Library/Application Support/ReuseRankClips/clips.json on your Mac. Nothing is sent anywhere, and only plain text is captured. Delete the file or use Clear Recent History to remove it.
Notarization requires a paid Apple Developer account, and this is a free project. Right-click the app and choose Open once to launch it, or build it yourself from source with Xcode.
